Investing.com -- MercadoLibre Inc (MELI) reported Q3 2026 on Nov 4. Revenue was strong, but EPS missed and margins shrank again. Shares were at $1,514.52 (-12.95%) as of Nov 5, 1:11 PM EST, near the low end of a 52-week range of $1,469.01–$2,342.

MercadoLibre Inc (MELI): $1,514.52 (Market Cap: ~$76.5B) || EPS $8.83 vs $9.34 est (-5.46%) || Revenue $10.75B vs $10.69B est (+45% YoY) || Operating margin 6.3% vs 12.2% a year earlier

Sources: Investing.com earnings report, Nov 4 and Nov 5 move.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Questions Answered

Is growth intact? Yes. GMV rose 38% to $23B and payment volume rose 53% to $109B. The company said it gained share in Brazil, Mexico and Argentina.

Is credit scaling? Yes. The portfolio is near $18B (+62% YoY). Fintech users grew 29% to 93M. Cantor said net interest margin after losses was stable despite record card issuance (Cantor note, Nov 5).

Is the balance sheet fine? It looks fine. The company completed a $1B investment-grade bond issue in September.

Do low-cost shipments pay? Raymond James noted they turned variable contribution positive for the first time (Nov 5).

Questions Still Open

Have margins bottomed? Operating margin fell from 7.0% last quarter to 6.3%. Net income was $448M (4.2% margin). Net shipping margin is down about 200 bps of GMV since Q1 2025.

What is driving the squeeze? Fulfillment square footage grew almost 20% QoQ. Free-shipping thresholds were lowered. Sales and marketing rose to 11.6% of revenue from 11.2% on Brazil's affiliate program.

Is Mexico slowing? FX-neutral GMV rose only 21%, with tax reform and weak consumption cited.

Is the miss a pattern? EPS missed in 3 of the last 4 quarters. The Q1 miss of -12.17% led to an -11.33% reaction.

Are new credit cohorts profitable? Per Raymond James, the 2026 Brazil card cohort is still loss-making and the 2025 cohort is at break-even.

Estimates Are Sliding

Consensus EPS is down 6.75% over 90 days and 33.37% over a year. Revenue estimates are up 15.29% over the same year. Analysts are paying for growth but are cutting their profit expectations.

Next Catalysts

Q4 results: tentatively Feb 25, 2027. Consensus is EPS $11.17 and revenue $11.96B. Peak-season fulfillment utilization will test whether margins stabilize.

Margin trajectory: Raymond James expects the investment cycle to ease as fulfillment utilization and slow-shipping economics improve. Cantor cut its FY2027 EBIT estimate on near-term investments.

Competition: the previous week's preview piece cited Chinese rivals gaining after the removal of the 20% import tax on items under $50. It also said Shopee has launched four-hour delivery in São Paulo (preview, Nov 4).

Credit seasoning: a slower ratio of new cards to aged cohorts would help the credit margin.

Analyst targets: targets were cut but ratings stayed bullish. Examples are Cantor at $2,000, Scotiabank at $2,300 and StoneX at $2,260.

MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) stock is down 13% today at about $1,515, after a third-quarter profit miss on Nov. 4. That leaves it down 34% over the past year.

MercadoLibre Spent Its Margin on Growth

After MercadoLibre cut Brazil's free-shipping threshold to R$19 from R$79 in June 2025 and ramped up credit card issuance, its operating margin fell to 6.7% in the second quarter of 2026, from 12.2% a year earlier.

Lula's surprise win in Brazil's Oct. 25 runoff sent Brazilian stocks lower, on fears of a weaker real. Brazil brought in 52.6% of MercadoLibre's 2025 revenue.

In the third quarter, revenue rose 45% to $10.75 billion (41% FX-neutral), but operating income fell 6.6% to $676 million, a 6.3% margin, and EPS of $8.83 missed the $9.27 consensus. title: MercadoLibre Pays Up to Win Shoppers’ Loyalty
detail:
MercadoLibre Pays Up to Win Shoppers’ Loyalty
The Rule Breakers Team, The Motley Fool

MELI
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

After the market closed yesterday, MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) reported third-quarter revenue of $10.75 billion, up 45% from a year ago. Operating income fell 6% to $676 million, and the operating margin shrank to 6.3% from 9.8% a year earlier. The stock fell about 6% in pre-market trading this morning.

Much of that lost profit went to shoppers. For Team Rule Breakers, which has recommended the stock twice in Stock Advisor since 2023, that choice is a direct test of what draws customers to a business and keeps them there.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The fifth of six Rule Breakers Traits is: Strong Consumer Appeal

Shoppers today face more choices than they can sort through. Brands that let people pick one trusted place to shop and pay can earn deep loyalty, and the best ones build raving fans. That loyalty rarely shows up in financial statements, which is one reason the market can overlook it.

Where the Profit Went

Last year, MercadoLibre lowered the order size needed for free shipping in Brazil. Shoppers responded by buying cheaper items more often. Items sold in Brazil rose 45% in the quarter, but each package now brings in less revenue. The company also grew its warehouse space by almost 20% in a single quarter ahead of the holiday season and spent more on affiliate marketing in Brazil. Management said it gained market share in Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina.

Its fintech business grew quickly, too. Monthly active users rose 29% to 93 million, and the credit portfolio grew 62% to nearly $18 billion. The company sets aside money for expected loan losses as soon as it extends a loan. Interest income arrives later, so fast credit growth tends to weigh on profit today.

When Perks Become Expectations

Once shoppers get used to free shipping, they may resist paying for it again. MercadoLibre could then struggle to restore its margins without losing some of the customers it just won. Rivals such as Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) also compete hard in Brazil, which makes pulling back on perks riskier.

The other markets and the lending business carry their own risks. In Mexico, tax changes and weaker spending slowed growth. Late loans held steady in the quarter, but a credit book growing this fast could cause trouble if Latin American borrowers come under strain.

Is the Appeal Worth the Price?

For patient holders, the bet is that today's spending is buying lasting habits. Shoppers who come to rely on fast, free delivery and a trusted place to pay may keep coming back long after the subsidies ease. The company gave no financial guidance, so the timing of any margin recovery is still unclear.

We're giving our own recommendations the same patience. Team Rule Breakers recommended MercadoLibre in Stock Advisor on Sept. 21, 2023, at $1,293.28, and again on Nov. 21, 2024, at $1,968.15. The first is up since then but trails the S&P 500, and the second is below its recommendation price.

We judge a stock over at least three to five years, so neither has had its full run yet. Across Motley Fool services, Team Rule Breakers and Team Hidden Gems have recommended MercadoLibre more than 50 times, and it has never been sold or moved to the Penalty Box.

Investors who believe MercadoLibre is building real loyalty may see this quarter as an opportunity to invest. Anyone less sure might wait for margins to steady.

Coupang (CPNG) stock rose 12.0% on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, while the S&P 500 gained 1.6%. The advance came the day after the e-commerce company reported third-quarter results on November 3, during a session where all five companies on its Trefis peer list also climbed. So what did Coupang's quarter show?

Coupang Beat Sales Estimates With Mixed Per-Share Results

Coupang's revenue reached $9.96 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, clearing the analysts' consensus estimate of $9.76 billion. Sales grew 7.5% from a year earlier. Measured at constant exchange rates, management put growth at 11%, exceeding the 8% to 9% range it had guided to.

Against estimates, the per-share results proved mixed. Coupang recorded $248 million in costs during the quarter from a July fire at one of its fulfillment centers. Including the fire, the company posted a loss of $0.28 per share. Excluding it, the loss was about $0.18 per share. That missed the $0.09 loss in our earnings calendar's consensus but beat the Zacks consensus of a $0.23 loss.

Management also discussed Product Commerce, its main retail business. The segment generated an adjusted EBITDA margin of 4.6%, down about 420 basis points from a year earlier. Management tied part of the decline to last year's data incident, after which some WOW members left. Management believes the third quarter was the low point for that margin and expects it to return to about pre-incident levels by the middle of 2027.

Did Coupang Rise Alone Or With Other Retailers?

Coupang climbed with other retailers, advancing further than any of its five Trefis peers. Etsy gained 7.1% and Amazon added 6.1% that session, and XLY, the SPDR fund for consumer discretionary stocks, rose 4.3%.

Where Does Coupang Stock Stand Now?

Such a large advance is rare for Coupang. Only one other session in the previous 365 days brought a gain at least this big: a 14.1% rise on June 11, 2026.

The stock remains far below where it traded a year ago. Coupang stock lost 46.9% over the twelve months to November 4, 2026, while the S&P 500 returned 14.9%. Its highest close during that period was $32.13 on November 4, 2025, and its lowest was $13.75 on September 28, 2026. The stock has climbed back part of the way over the past month, returning 18.2% from October 6 to November 4 while the S&P 500 lost 1.6%.

Coupang's next report will cover the fourth quarter of 2026. Management expects revenue growth of 13% to 14% at constant exchange rates for that quarter, and that growth rate is the number to watch.

MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) stock is down 9% today after its third-quarter profit missed estimates. Management's explanation for the shrinking shipping margin? It's "the price of the habit."

That habit is being built on Brazil's low-priced orders, the ones Sea Limited (SE:NYSE) chases with Shopee. And the quarter's steady credit sets a bar for Nu Holdings (NU:NYSE).

Where the profit went

Revenue rose 45% to $10.75 billion, ahead of estimates. But EPS missed as operating income fell 6% to $676 million on more free shipping, almost 20% more fulfillment space ahead of the holidays, and extra affiliate marketing in Brazil.

Analysts expected margins to drive a rebound:

Paying for the habit

MercadoLibre cut Brazil's free shipping threshold to R$19 from R$79 in June 2025, and items sold there have grown more than 40% for five straight quarters since.

But cheaper items earn less each, so net shipping margin has lost about 200 basis points of gross merchandise volume since early 2025.

The margin was sliding well before the third quarter, when it fell to 6.3% from 9.8%:

Brazil's cost per shipment fell 5% from a year earlier in local currency. And in September, free, slow shipments priced from R$19 to R$79 covered their variable costs as a group for the first time.

That push lands on Shopee, whose Brazil capacity Sea grew 60% in a year. If Shopee's Brazil growth slows next week, MercadoLibre's shipping spend is buying share.

Credit held up, too: MercadoLibre's 15-90 day NPL stayed around 7.0%. Nu's improved to 4.8% in the second quarter, and its report next week will show whether its Brazil book is as steady.

MELI Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Growth and Margin Trade-Offs
Zacks Equity Research

Trade MELI on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

MercadoLibre, Inc. MELI emphasized sustained investments in e-commerce, logistics and financial services during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call. Management highlighted strong customer engagement and market-share gains across Latin America while defending its strategy of sacrificing near-term margins to support long-term growth.

CEO Ariel Szarfsztejn and CFO Martin de Los Santos maintained that growing transaction frequency, logistics efficiencies and deeper integration between commerce and fintech remain central to improving future profitability.

MercadoLibre reported third-quarter earnings of $8.83 per share, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $9.41. Earnings increased from $8.32 per share in the year-ago quarter. Net revenues and financial income surged 45% year over year to $10.75 billion, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $10.66 billion.

MercadoLibre, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise
MercadoLibre, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

MercadoLibre, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | MercadoLibre, Inc. Quote

MELI Defends Investments Despite Margin Pressure

Operating income declined 6% year over year to $676 million, while operating margin contracted 40 basis points sequentially to 6.3%. Management attributed the pressure primarily to higher shipping costs and affiliate marketing investments.

De Los Santos explained that lower free-shipping thresholds encouraged smaller, more frequent purchases, reducing revenue per shipment. Higher energy costs and expanded fulfillment capacity added further pressure.

During the Q&A, an FT Partners analyst questioned the sustainability of these costs. De Los Santos indicated that some capacity-related expenses should ease in the fourth quarter, while higher fuel costs could persist. Management reiterated that it prioritizes long-term engagement over short-term margin expansion.

MercadoLibre Sees Strong Momentum in Brazil

Brazil remained a major growth driver, with foreign exchange-neutral gross merchandise volume increasing 36% year over year. Items sold climbed 45%, reflecting continued benefits from lower free-shipping thresholds.

De Los Santos highlighted a 16% increase in items purchased per buyer. Brazil's cost per shipment declined 5% year over year in local currency, reflecting improving logistics efficiency despite infrastructure expansion.

Management also reported nearly 20% sequential growth in fulfillment capacity across its network. Responding to a Santander analyst, De Los Santos explained that the additional infrastructure supports both holiday demand and anticipated longer-term growth.

MELI Expands Social Commerce and Advertising

A Morgan Stanley analyst questioned whether increased affiliate marketing spending represented a structural change in MercadoLibre's customer acquisition strategy.

Szarfsztejn explained that social platforms increasingly influence product discovery, making affiliate marketing an important additional acquisition channel. However, he expects organic traffic to remain the primary source of marketplace activity.

De Los Santos clarified that the recent spending increase was tactical, although affiliate marketing remains a strategic priority. Orders through the channel grew 240% year over year, while the affiliate network exceeded 12 million participants. Advertising revenues increased 58% in U.S. dollars.

MercadoLibre Prioritizes Credit Quality Amid Expansion

Mercado Pago's monthly active users increased 29% year over year to 93 million, while the credit portfolio expanded 62% to nearly $18 billion.

Fintech President Osvaldo Giménez told a JPMorgan analyst that management had become marginally more cautious in riskier Brazilian lending segments. Nevertheless, the portfolio's 15-to-90-day nonperforming loan ratio remained stable at 7%.

Credit-card expansion continued to influence profitability, with net interest margin after losses reaching 20.1%. Giménez explained that newer card cohorts initially pressure returns because provisions precede interest income, while mature Brazilian cohorts are generating positive contributions.

MELI Highlights AI as an Efficiency Driver

Management emphasized artificial intelligence as an increasingly important contributor to customer engagement, advertising performance and operational productivity.

Responding to a Raymond James analyst, De Los Santos explained that incremental revenues from AI-enhanced search exceeded the associated model costs. He also highlighted improved developer productivity and customer support efficiency.

Szarfsztejn clarified that MercadoLibre currently prioritizes developing its own AI shopping assistant rather than sharing marketplace inventory with external platforms. The company is testing its agentic shopping experience with selected users across its three largest markets.

MercadoLibre Maintains Its Long-Term Growth Focus

Management reiterated its commitment to strengthening the commerce-fintech ecosystem through customer engagement, logistics improvements and disciplined reinvestment. Szarfsztejn emphasized that rising purchase frequency and deeper financial relationships should support greater operating efficiency over time.

The company continues balancing infrastructure expansion and customer acquisition investments against margin pressures. Management maintained that improving cost-to-serve economics and expanding ecosystem participation remain central to its long-term profitability strategy.

What Do Zacks Rank and Style Scores Indicate for MELI?

MercadoLibre currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), indicating a neutral near-term earnings estimate revision outlook. eBay (EBAY) stock returned 55.2% in the year to November 4, 2026, against 14.9% for the S&P 500. eBay's sales growth picked up sharply over those months. On the October 28, 2026 call, management pointed to consumers selling to each other and to the categories it chose to focus on, such as collectibles, motors and fashion. So when did that growth first show up where you could have seen it?

eBay Showed The First Signs In February 2025

That first sign arrived on eBay's February 26, 2025 call for the fourth quarter of 2024. Management said its focus category volume grew 5% in 2024, while gross merchandise volume, the value of goods sold across the whole marketplace, grew by just over 1%. During the same call, management described an overhaul of selling between consumers in the U.K., its second-largest market. Those are the same two areas management pointed to in October 2026. Yet eBay's revenue had grown only 0.7% in the quarter ended December 2024, so the sign was easy to dismiss.

In 2025, eBay's revenue growth picked up in each quarter, moving from 1.1% in the quarter ended March to 6.1% in the quarter ended June. On October 30, 2025, eBay filed its report for the quarter ended September with revenue up 9.5% from a year earlier. That filing arrived days before the twelve months measured here began.

eBay stock was already rising by then, gaining 21.5% in the six months before November 3, 2025. So the signs could be read in public. Anyone who waited for the September quarter's filing bought late in that rise, but still before the run measured here began.

eBay's Revenue Growth More Than Tripled In A Year

eBay's revenue grew 15.7% in the four quarters to September 2026, against 4.4% in the four quarters before. Over the run, eBay stock beat three of its peers: Walmart returned 27.4%, Amazon 6.7% and MercadoLibre fell 24.5%.

During the October 28, 2026 call, management said its focus categories, consumer-to-consumer selling and recommerce, the resale of used goods, together grew merchandise volume by about 20% in the third quarter. Those businesses now make up 72% of eBay's merchandise volume, excluding Depop, the consumer-to-consumer fashion marketplace eBay finished buying on July 30, 2026. Management singled out two of those three areas in February 2025.

Are eBay's Focus Categories Still Growing Faster Today?

Yes. Management said focus category volume grew 24% in the third quarter of 2026, outpacing the rest of the marketplace by 19 percentage points. Collectibles, motors, fashion and refurbished goods all added to growth.

Logistics network efficiency improved, with cost per shipment in Brazil declining 5% year on year on an FX-neutral basis and 14% since lowering the free shipping threshold.

Negative Points

Sales and marketing expenses rose 40 basis points sequentially to 11.6% of net revenue, reflecting increased investment in the affiliate program in Brazil.

Credit portfolio growth may face pressure from a weaker credit environment in Brazil and Argentina, requiring caution in riskier segments.

The company expects continued investment in areas like affiliates and logistics capacity, which may weigh on margins in the near term.
